chain: boot progress observability for structural walk + replay
Contributed by Ziyang (as exfer-stack) upstream to ahuman-exfer/exfer, the Exfer chain itself.
https://github.com/ahuman-exfer/exfer/pull/24

Motivation

On a marker-less or pre-3a datadir, boot runs two full-chain passes that can each take many minutes on slow / network-attached storage: the structural walk in `open_chain` and `replay_chain`. The walk was effectively silent — it logged `running full structural walk` and then nothing until completion. An operator tailing the logs during a long boot (e.g. a fresh deploy restored from an older volume snapshot) cannot tell whether it is advancing, how far along it is, or when it will finish, and a CPU-bound walk is indistinguishable from a hang without `/proc` forensics.

Observed live: a v1.11.9 node booted from a clone of a pre-3a / pre-#16 volume (~672k blocks) sat in the structural walk for 20+ minutes with zero log output. The process was healthy (state R, climbing utime + minflt) but that could only be confirmed by inspecting `/proc/<pid>/stat` over SSH — not acceptable observability for an operator.

Change

- Structural walk (`open_chain`): log the verify range up front, then every 1000 blocks (and on the final block) report `done/total (pct) at height H · blk/s · elapsed · ETA`.
- `replay_chain`: the existing every-1000 progress line now also carries blocks/s and ETA (previously elapsed seconds only).

Pure logging — no behavioural change. Both paths throttle at 1000 blocks, so log volume stays bounded regardless of chain length. Identical format across the two phases so a full cold boot (walk then replay) reads as one continuous progress stream.
